facts.statement: Cardiodon is a herbivorous sauropod genus known from a single tooth found in the Middle Jurassic Forest Marble Formation of Wiltshire, England.
facts.quote: Cardiodon (meaning "heart tooth", in reference to the shape) was a herbivorous genus of sauropod dinosaur, based on a tooth from the Middle Jurassic (late Bathonian) Forest Marble Formation of Wiltshire, England.

facts.statement: Richard Owen assigned the specific name rugulosus, meaning "wrinkled", to the species in 1844.
facts.quote: A few years later, in 1844, he added the specific name rugulosus, meaning "wrinkled" in Latin.

facts.statement: Cardiodon was the first sauropod genus to receive a formal name, although the describer was unaware of its classification at the time.
facts.quote: Cardiodon was the first sauropod given a formal name to, though Owen was at the time completely unaware of the sauropod nature of the find.

facts.statement: Fossils of Cardiodon were found in the Forest Marble and Great Oolite formations near Wiltshire and Gloucestershire, England.
facts.quote: El cardiodón fue encontrado en Forest Marble, Wiltshire, en la Formación Great Oolite, cerca de Gloucestershire, Inglaterra.

facts.statement: Cardiodon rugulosus lived approximately 167 million years ago during the Middle Jurassic Bathonian stage in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: Cardiodon rugulosus (gr. "diente en corazón arrugado") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Cardiodon de dinosaurio saurópodo turiasauriano, que vivió a mediados el período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 167 millones de años, en el Bathoniense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: The genus Cardiodon existed between 168.2 and 165.3 million years ago during the Bathonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Bathonian (168.2 to 165.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Recent analyses suggest Cardiodon is a distinct genus possibly related to Turiasaurus, though it was historically often referred to as Cetiosaurus.
facts.quote: Historically, it is very obscure and usually referred to Cetiosaurus, but recent analyses suggest that it is a distinct genus, and possibly related to Turiasaurus.

facts.statement: Cardiodon was previously classified within the Cetiosauridae family or its own family, Cardiodontidae.
facts.quote: Anteriormente, Cardiodon había sido asignado normalmente a los Cetiosauridae o a su propia familia Cardiodontidae.

facts.statement: The known tooth of Cardiodon is spatulate with a slight convexity on its inner side, a rare combination.
facts.quote: The original tooth shows, as far as can be deduced from the surviving illustrations, the rare combination of being spatulate and having a convex inner side, though the convexity is slight.

facts.statement: Cardiodon teeth differ from Cetiosaurus teeth because they possess a convex lingual face.
facts.quote: Los dientes se diferencian del de Cetiosaurus, debido a que presenta la cara lingual convexa.

facts.statement: The tooth crown is short and wide, slightly curved inward, with an outer side strongly convex from front to rear.
facts.quote: Su corona es corta y ancha, ligeramente curvada hacia el interior. El lado exterior es fuertemente convexo curvado de la parte delantera a la parte trasera.

facts.statement: A shallow groove runs parallel to the rear edge on the outer side of the tooth crown.
facts.quote: En este lado está presente una ranura poco profunda, paralela al borde trasero.

facts.statement: The tooth crown tapers toward its tip and lacks denticles on its edges.
facts.quote: La corona se estrecha hacia su punta. Los bordes no tienen dentículos.

facts.statement: The enamel of the tooth shows small wrinkles, which is the feature referenced by the specific name rugulosus.
facts.quote: El esmalte muestra las pequeñas arrugas a las que se refiere el nombre específico.

facts.statement: As a sauropod, Cardiodon was likely a large, quadrupedal herbivore, though scanty remains limit further details.
facts.quote: As a sauropod, Cardiodon would have been a large, quadrupedal herbivore, but because of the scanty remains, much more cannot be said.

facts.statement: Although only known from teeth, a probable body length of 16 meters has been estimated for Cardiodon.
facts.quote: Cardiodon solo se lo conoce por sus dientes, pero se ha aventurado un tamaño probable de 16 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Researchers Upchurch and Martin (2003) argued that Cardiodon should be retained as a distinct genus because the teeth differ from those of Cetiosaurus oxoniensis and lack evidence linking them to that skeleton.
facts.quote: In 2003, Paul Upchurch and John Martin, reviewing Cetiosaurus, found that there is little evidence to assign the C. oxoniensis teeth to the skeleton, and the "C. oxoniensis" teeth differ from the Cardiodon teeth (Cardiodon teeth are convex facing the tongue); therefore, they supported Cardiodon being retained as its own genus.

facts.statement: Upchurch et al. (2004) found that Cardiodon teeth possess autapomorphies distinct from those of eusauropods, supporting its separation.
facts.quote: Upchurch et al. en 2004 revisaron lo conocido y encontraron que los dientes de Cardiodon presentan autapomorfias, con los de los eusaurópodos.

rejected.statement: Richard Owen named the genus Cardiodon in 1841 based on a lost tooth from the collection of Joseph Chaning Pearce found near Bradford-on-Avon.
rejected.quote: Richard Owen named the genus for a now-lost tooth, part of the collection of naturalist Joseph Chaning Pearce, found near Bradford-on-Avon, but did not assign it a specific name at the time.
